content.antithrombotic_strategy: Preference for a NOAC over VKA for default strategy when no contraindications. For both TAT and DAT regimens, recommended NOAC doses listed; NOAC dose reductions based on renal function, body weight, concomitant meds and age.
content.SAPT_recommendation: Preference for a P2Y12 receptor inhibitor (usually clopidogrel) over aspirin for single antiplatelet therapy (SAPT).
content.DAT_TAT_duration: DAT may be shortened to 6 months by withdrawing antiplatelet therapy in certain patients; TAT may be prolonged up to 1 month followed by DAT for up to 12 months in high ischemic risk patients.
content.ticagrelor_prasugrel_note: Limited evidence to support use of OAC with ticagrelor or prasugrel as DAT after ACS/PCI; ticagrelor and prasugrel were used in small percentages in pivotal RCTs.
content.medically_managed_ACS: Current data support DAT over TAT with a single antiplatelet agent (most commonly clopidogrel) for at least 6 months in medically managed ACS patients.
content.AUGUSTUS_trial: In AUGUSTUS, apixaban reduced bleeding events vs VKA in medically managed ACS patients; no significant differences in death or ischaemic events.
content.AFIRE_trial: AFIRE randomized AF patients with prior PCI/CABG or documented CAD to rivaroxaban monotherapy vs combination; rivaroxaban monotherapy was non-inferior for efficacy and superior for major bleeding, supporting stopping antiplatelet therapy after 12 months and continuing OAC monotherapy in most patients.

Associated Conditions: Single antiplatelet therapy (SAPT) preference over aspirin
genes.context: SAPT: preference for a P2Y12 receptor inhibitor (usually clopidogrel) over aspirin.
